description: Historically supported relations between 1444 entities, keyed by country-catalogue ids. A missing pair means nothing is recorded, not Neutral.

relations.expiration_condition: Original term; history extended it to 1449.

historical_end.how: France resumed war after the English sack of Fougères (March 1449).

relations.explanation: Truce of Tours ended open war in the Hundred Years' War and was tied to the betrothal of Henry VI to Margaret of Anjou. Extended several times; fighting resumed in 1449.
The English king claims the French crown and holds Normandy, Maine and Guyenne; both sides contest the same lands.
The Franco-Scottish alliance, renewed in 1428 and sealed by the 1436 marriage of Margaret Stewart to the dauphin Louis.
Long-standing Trastámara-Valois alliance, renewed under Juan II and Charles VII; Castilian fleets had served France.
Nine-year Anglo-Scottish truce concluded during James II's minority; border raiding continued underneath it.
Scotland seeks to recover Roxburgh and Berwick; England claims overlordship. Contested border fortresses.
Treaty of Windsor: perpetual alliance, still observed in the 1440s.
After Burgundy left the English alliance (Arras, 1435) and besieged Calais (1436), a commercial truce covering Flanders was agreed at Gravelines and renewed.

relations.note: Burgundy's legal vassalage for its French fiefs is suspended in 1444; see uncertainty report.
relations.explanation: Valois Burgundy and the French crown compete for power after the Armagnac-Burgundian civil war; Philip the Good was exempted from homage for life by the Treaty of Arras, so no subject relation is stored.
Montfort dukes owe homage to the French king; whether it was liege homage was disputed.
René of Anjou holds Anjou as a royal apanage and sits in Charles VII's council.
Charles of Orléans, released from English captivity in 1440, holds his duchy as a prince of the blood.
Charles I of Bourbon, a prince of the blood; submitted after the Praguerie (1440).
John II of Alençon, royal vassal and former Praguerie rebel.
Count Jean IV was captured by royal forces in 1443 and his lands put under royal control until 1445.
Gaston IV holds Foix from the French crown and serves Charles VII; Béarn is held separately in full sovereignty.
Lords of Albret, royal vassals in Gascony fighting the English.
County held by a Burgundian cadet line as a French fief.
Group record of lesser royal vassals.
Apanage of the heir, the dauphin Louis.
René of Anjou, count of Provence, is Charles VII's brother-in-law and campaigned with him at Metz in 1444.
Angevins and Alfonso V fought for Naples; René lost Naples in 1442 and kept the claim.

relations.expiration_condition: Peace treaty; superseded by Franco-Swiss agreements of 1452-53.
relations.explanation: Treaty of Ensisheim after the battle of St. Jakob an der Birs (26 Aug 1444) ended the dauphin's campaign against the Confederates.

historical_end.how: Metz paid an indemnity and the siege was lifted.

relations.explanation: Charles VII and René of Anjou besieged Metz from September 1444; the city bought peace in 1445.
The siege of Metz arose from René's claims as duke of Lorraine against the city.
Bar and Lorraine both held by René of Anjou and Isabella of Lorraine.
Counts of Vaudemont, René's former rivals (1431), reconciled by marriage in 1444-45 but holding Vaudemont from the duke.
English-held Normandy, Maine and Guyenne, governed by the king's lieutenants.
The English king is Lord of Ireland; the lordship has its own parliament and administration.
The Stanleys hold Man from the English crown.
Butler earls of Ormond, magnates and sometime lieutenants of the lordship.
FitzGerald earls of Desmond: Anglo-Irish earls, largely gaelicised and only loosely bound.
Alexander MacDonald, Lord of the Isles and earl of Ross, holds from the Scottish crown and served as justiciar north of the Forth.
The Black Douglas earldom dominates southern Scotland during James II's minority.
William Sinclair holds the earldom of Orkney from the Norwegian crown.
MacMurrough Kavanagh raids the Pale borders and extracts protection payments.
O'Neill of Tyrone presses the Ulster earldom lands and the Pale with raids and black rent.
O'Donnell and O'Neill compete for dominance in Ulster and over the lesser lords between them.
Desmond and the O'Briens of Thomond contend for Munster.
County held by Philip the Good since 1419. Each keeps its estates and privileges inside the Burgundian composite state.
Duchy inherited by Philip in 1430. Each keeps its estates and privileges inside the Burgundian composite state.
Holland and Zeeland ceded by Jacqueline of Bavaria in 1433. Each keeps its estates and privileges inside the Burgundian composite state.
County ceded with Holland in 1433. Each keeps its estates and privileges inside the Burgundian composite state.
Philip took Luxembourg by surprise in November 1443 under an agreement with Elisabeth of Görlitz; the Saxon and Habsburg claims stayed open.
The great Flemish city, privileged and restive inside the county (revolt of 1449-53).
Adolf I of Cleves married Mary of Burgundy; John of Cleves was raised at Philip's court.

historical_end.how: Papal mediation; Soest stayed with Cleves.

relations.explanation: Soest Feud: Cleves took Soest under its lordship and Archbishop Dietrich of Moers went to war.
Soest renounced the archbishop's lordship and was attacked in the Soest Feud.

relations.note: The catalogue lists Soest's overlord as Cologne (contested); see uncertainty report.
relations.explanation: Soest accepted John of Cleves as its lord on 5 June 1444.
County of Mark joined to Cleves under one house; contested by Gerhard of Cleves-Mark.
Dietrich of Moers, archbishop of Cologne, also administers Paderborn.
Heinrich of Moers, bishop of Münster, administers Osnabrück.
The sees are held by the brothers Dietrich and Heinrich of Moers.
Peace of Copenhagen ended the Dutch-Wendish war with a ten-year truce between Holland-Zeeland and the Wendish towns led by Lübeck.
Truces with Castile carried parias in gold, paid irregularly amid Nasrid succession strife; frontier raiding continued.

relations.note: Whether fighting or a truce held on 11 Nov 1444 is unresolved; see uncertainty report.
relations.explanation: Prince Henry and Álvaro de Luna declared war on Juan of Navarre and the Infantes of Aragon in March 1444; Navarre invaded in 1445 and lost at Olmedo.
The Infantes of Aragon contest power in Castile with Alfonso V's backing.

relations.note: The catalogue records an alliance; no binding war treaty is attested, so it is stored as Friendly.
relations.explanation: Treaty of Medina del Campo ended the war of 1383-1411; regent Pedro sent troops to aid Juan II in 1445.
State of war since Portugal took Ceuta; the 1437 Tangier capitulation (Ceuta for Prince Fernando) was never carried out.
Ceuta held by a Portuguese captain since 1415.
Afonso, duke of Braganza, leads the noble opposition to regent Pedro.
Santiago, Calatrava and Alcántara under royal patronage; masterships fought over.
Great noble lineages holding seigneurial jurisdictions.
The seigneurs of the conquered Canaries hold them as a Castilian fief.
Raids and failed conquest attempts against the guanarteme polities of Gran Canaria.
Slave raids from the seigneurial islands on Tenerife.
Slave raids from the seigneurial islands on La Palma.
Constituent kingdom with its own Cortes and Justicia.
Constituent principality with Corts and Generalitat.
Constituent kingdom with Corts and Generalitat.
Sicily ruled by Aragonese viceroys.
Kingdom of Sardinia under the Crown of Aragon.
Marquisate of Oristano, the Arborean heirs' fief under the Aragonese crown.
Treaty of Terracina: Eugenius IV invested Alfonso with Naples, a papal fief owing census, and Alfonso undertook to help recover the Marche for the Church.
Giovanni Antonio Orsini del Balzo, the realm's greatest baron.

relations.note: Treaty date given as 15 or 19 February 1444.
relations.explanation: Stjepan Vukčić Kosača became Alfonso V's vassal by treaty in exchange for help against his enemies.
Doge Raffaele Adorno accepted peace with Alfonso, recognising him as king of Naples with an annual symbolic gift.
Competition over Corsica, Sardinia and western Mediterranean trade.
Juan of Navarre is Alfonso's brother and his lieutenant-general in Aragon.
Co-principality shared by the counts of Foix and the bishops of Urgell under the paréages.
Este papal vicars for Ferrara (Modena and Reggio are imperial fiefs).
Montefeltro papal vicars; Oddantonio was made duke in 1443 and murdered in July 1444.
Sigismondo Malatesta, papal vicar and condottiere.
Galeazzo Malatesta, papal vicar (sold Pesaro to the Sforza in 1445).
Varano lords, restored in the 1440s as papal vicars.
Manfredi papal vicars.
Ordelaffi papal vicars.
Group of minor papal vicariates in Romagna.
Bologna under the Bentivoglio, papal in law but ruling itself and allied with Venice and Florence.
Maritime commune under papal sovereignty paying a census.
Colonna, Orsini and other baronial houses of Lazio.
Papal enclave around Avignon.

historical_end.how: War renewed; Sforza lost most of the Marche by 1446.

relations.explanation: After Sforza beat the Church's and Visconti's captains in 1444, Eugenius IV made peace confirming most of his hold on the Marche; the pope renewed the war in 1445.
League of Venice and Florence against Milan, repeatedly renewed.
Florence and Cosimo de' Medici subsidised Sforza.
Venice backed Sforza against the Visconti-papal coalition in the Marche.
Lombard wars over Brescia, Bergamo and the Adda frontier; peace of Cavriana (1441) did not settle them.
Florence opposes Visconti hegemony in central and northern Italy.
Filippo Maria Visconti turned against his son-in-law and sent Piccinino against him in the Marche.
The rump Council of Basel deposed Eugenius IV and elected Felix V.
Amadeus VIII of Savoy is the anti-pope Felix V; his son Duke Louis upholds his obedience.
Asti came to the Orléans line as Valentina Visconti's dowry and is ruled by Orléans governors.
Florence's failed war of conquest (1429-38) left Lucca guarding its independence.

historical_end.how: Truce after Varna; war resumed with the 1448 Kosovo campaign.

relations.explanation: Crusade of Varna: the peace of Edirne-Szeged was repudiated and the crusading army was destroyed at Varna on 10 November 1444; war continued.
Vlad II Dracul sent troops under his son Mircea to join the crusade.
Joint crusade campaign of 1444 (and the Danube expedition of 1445).
The papacy financed and its legate Cesarini led the crusade alongside the Hungarian king.
Papal galleys formed the core of the crusading fleet at the Straits.
The Venetian fleet sent to the Straits to cut Ottoman crossings; separate peace in 1446.
Burgundian galleys under Waleran de Wavrin sailed with the crusade fleet and campaigned on the Danube in 1445.
Byzantium paid annual tribute to the Ottomans under the 1424 treaty.
Despotate of the Morea held by the emperor's brothers Constantine and Thomas.
Constantine forced Nerio II Acciaioli to pay him tribute in 1444; the Ottomans restored their suzerainty in 1446.

historical_end.how: Murad stormed the Hexamilion; the despots paid tribute.

relations.explanation: Constantine rebuilt the Hexamilion and pushed into Ottoman-held central Greece while the crusade was under way.
The peace of 1444 restored Đurađ Branković's despotate as an Ottoman tributary owing troops and tribute.
Bosnian kings paid tribute to the sultan from the 1430s.

historical_end.how: Stephen Thomas married Kosača's daughter Katarina.

relations.explanation: Civil war between King Stephen Thomas and Stjepan Vukčić Kosača, ended by a marriage settlement in 1446.
Albanian lords leagued under Skanderbeg defeated an Ottoman army at Torvioll on 29 June 1444.
Ragusa owes the Hungarian crown tribute and recognition since the peace of Zadar.
Cyprus became a Mamluk tributary after the defeat at Khirokitia.
Mamluk expeditions against Rhodes in 1440 and 1444; the 1444 siege was lifted in September with no peace yet.
The Maona company governs Chios under Genoese sovereignty.
Caffa and the Genoese Black Sea towns, ruled by a consul sent from Genoa.
Pera and other Genoese Aegean holdings.
Theodoro and Genoese Caffa fought over Cembalo in 1433-34.
Hacı Giray and Theodoro acted together against the Genoese in 1434.
Hacı Giray came to power from Lithuanian exile with Casimir's consent.
Karaman contests Ottoman primacy in Anatolia; Ibrahim Bey attacked in 1444 in step with the crusade.
Murad II's 1444 campaign forced Ibrahim Bey of Karaman to make peace before the sultan turned to the crusade.
Union of Florence: the papacy organised the crusade to relieve Constantinople.
Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia under the Hungarian crown.
Voivodeship held by John Hunyadi.
Jan Jiskra holds Upper Hungary for the infant Ladislaus V against Władysław's party.
Jiskra serves the Habsburg claimant held by Frederick III.
Frederick III holds the Holy Crown, the child Ladislaus V and pledged western Hungarian towns against Władysław's regime.
Frederick III and the counts of Cilli concluded a mutual succession treaty.
Zurich allied with Frederick III against the other Confederates.
Old Zurich War: Habsburg fought the Confederates on Zurich's side.

relations.note: Zurich remains a catalogue member of the Confederation; membership is not a relation here.
relations.explanation: Old Zurich War over the Toggenburg inheritance; Zurich besieged in 1444.
Mazovian Piast duchy held as a fief of the Polish crown.
Mazovian Piast duchy held as a fief of the Polish crown.
Moldavian voivodes did homage to the Polish king; Stephen II ruled after blinding his brother Ilie in 1443.
Švitrigaila holds Volhynia for life after reconciling with Casimir.
After Lithuania raised Casimir unilaterally (1440) the union lapsed; Podolia and Volhynia were disputed until 1447.
Unsettled frontier disputes after the eternal peace of Brześć Kujawski (1435).
Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order with its own master.
Prince-bishopric under the Order's protection.
Neumark pledged to the Order by the Luxembourgs.
League of Prussian towns and knights formed at Marienwerder to defend its rights against the Order.
The estates' league resists the Order's taxation and justice; it rose in 1454.
Riga city submitted to the Order in 1330.
Bishopric of Courland incorporated with the Order.
The archbishops of Riga dispute lordship over Riga and Livonia with the Order.
Livonian-Novgorodian war over the Narva frontier.
Land or estate of the Bohemian crown during the interregnum of 1439-53.
Land or estate of the Bohemian crown during the interregnum of 1439-53.

Utraquist and Catholic regional leagues contest control of Bohemia.
Poděbrady's Utraquists oppose radical Tábor, taken in 1452.
Dispute over the Uckermark, fought 1444/45-1448 and settled at Prenzlau.
Albrecht Achilles and Nuremberg contest rights in Franconia (war of 1449).
Adolf VIII of Holstein enfeoffed with Schleswig as a hereditary fief by Christopher of Bavaria.
Christopher of Bavaria, Danish king, accepted as Swedish king by the riksråd.
Christopher crowned king of Norway; the union king resides in Denmark.
Iceland under the Norwegian crown since the Old Covenant.
The Faroes under the Norwegian crown.
Deposed king Eric of Pomerania holds Visby and preys on Baltic shipping.
Eric's Gotland privateers attack Hanseatic shipping.
First Russo-Kazan war; Ulugh Muhammad's forces took Nizhny Novgorod in 1444-45 and captured Vasily II at Suzdal in 1445.

relations.note: An appanage prince competing with the grand prince for the throne.
relations.explanation: Dynastic war for the Muscovite throne; Shemyaka seized Moscow in 1446.
Ivan Andreyevich of Mozhaysk holds an appanage of the Moscow house.
Mikhail Andreyevich holds Vereya and Beloozero as an appanage.
Vasily II campaigned against Novgorod in 1441 and extracted a payment.
Sharifs of Mecca appointed and confirmed by the Mamluk sultan.
Amirs of Medina under Mamluk authority.
Dulkadir beys of Elbistan hold their beylik as Mamluk clients.
Ramadanid emirs of Adana under Mamluk suzerainty.
The Turkmen confederations fight over eastern Anatolia and Azerbaijan.
Jahan Shah held Azerbaijan by Shah Rukh's grant and acknowledged him until 1447.
Jahan Shah invaded Georgia in 1440 and sacked Samshvilde.
Shirvanshah Khalilullah I acknowledged Shah Rukh.
Ulugh Beg governs Transoxiana for his father Shah Rukh.
Fars held by a Timurid prince under Shah Rukh.
Moghul raids on Transoxiana and Ulugh Beg's punitive expeditions.
Esen Taishi's Oirat campaigned against Moghulistan.
Tahirids rose in the Rasulid lowlands and replaced them by 1454.
The Sharqis of Jaunpur aim at Delhi itself; Mahmud Sharqi attacked in 1452.
Gujarat and Malwa sultans fought repeatedly over Malwa's succession and frontier.
Mahmud Khalji's campaigns against Rana Kumbha (Kumbhalgarh 1443, Mandalgarh 1446).
Rana Kumbha seized Mandore; Rao Jodha fought from exile to recover it (1453).
Recurring wars over the Raichur doab.
Ala-ud-din Ahmad II's war with Deva Raya II ended in a settlement in 1443.
The Zamorins of Calicut and the rulers of Cochin compete on the Malabar coast.
Esen Taishi's growing power and disputes over the tribute trade led to the Tumu crisis of 1449.
Taisun Khan reigns with the Oirat taishi Esen holding real power.
Joseon kings received Ming investiture and sent regular embassies.
The Shō kings received Ming investiture and traded under the tribute system.
Lê kings were invested as kings of Annam by the Ming after 1431.
Malacca's rulers were invested by the Ming and sent missions.
Champa sent tribute and sought Ming support against Dai Viet.
Jianzhou Jurchen guards under Ming titles.
Haixi Jurchen guards under Ming titles.
Hami guard under Ming titles, pressed by the Oirat.

Yang family pacification commission of Bozhou.
An family pacification commission of Shuixi.
Mu family native prefecture of Lijiang.
Luchuan-Pingmian campaigns against Si Renfa and his sons.
Ava fought Si Renfa and handed him to the Ming in 1445-46.
Rinpung lords hold Tsang as Phagmodrupa ministers while gaining real power.

Joseon campaigns against the Jurchen and the northern garrisons of the 1430s-40s.
Sukhothai absorbed into Ayutthaya under a royal viceroy at Phitsanulok.
Ayutthaya sacked Angkor in 1431; border wars continued.
Ayutthaya's attack on Lan Na in 1442 opened a long war.
Border wars; Dai Viet took Vijaya in 1446.
Prome under an Ava-appointed governor of the royal house.
Rival sultanates of the clove islands.
The Bulala drove the Sayfawa from Kanem; the struggle continued until c.1500.
The Kano Chronicle names Abdullahi Burja as the first Kano ruler to pay tribute to Bornu.
